objective: Continuously acquire qualified human traffic from existing demand and borrowed audiences, convert that traffic into software decisions and monetized outbound, and reallocate resources only from measured outcomes.

plays.title: SERP zero-click capture
plays.hypothesis: Search impressions that are already visible but not earning clicks can be converted faster by improving click capture, deepening the decision asset and amplifying the same intent externally.

plays.title: Authority publisher outreach
plays.hypothesis: Publisher and directory opportunities can produce new referring domains faster when contact discovery, reference outreach and backlink verification are treated as one automated acquisition play.

plays.title: Distribution surface family expansion
plays.hypothesis: When acquisition throughput is below target, ToolScout should expand into additional qualified external surface families instead of repeating the current route mix.

plays.title: Vendor co-distribution flywheel
plays.hypothesis: Vendors have existing audiences. Automatically packaging ToolScout reviews, comparisons and mentions for relevant vendor amplification can borrow that audience and create referral traffic and links.

plays.title: Ranking cluster compounding
plays.hypothesis: Search assets with observed demand should reinforce one another through stronger internal links, deeper decision coverage and external amplification rather than being optimized in isolation.

plays.title: Timely software-demand capture
plays.hypothesis: Verified software changes can be turned into timely search and borrowed-audience acquisition by publishing the search angle and amplifying it through the vendor while interest is fresh.

plays.title: Index recovery plus external amplification
plays.hypothesis: Pages already worth repairing for Google should receive distribution support in the same cycle so technical recovery is paired with external discovery signals.

plays.title: Proven surface scaling
plays.hypothesis: Any external surface already showing evidence should be scaled while new surfaces continue to be explored, instead of replacing exploration with exploitation.
